units.source: Accessing via the backend log__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Backend (server) logs > Accessing via the backend log

units.source: In the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Global menu__TRILIUM_PH_1__, go to __TRILIUM_PH_2__Advanced__TRILIUM_PH_3__ → __TRILIUM_PH_4__Backend log__TRILIUM_PH_5__. This will display the current backend log (i.e. today's), with the historical information available only on disk (see below).
units.context: Backend (server) logs > Accessing via the backend log

units.source: The log is colored to make it easier to read: request status codes by class, slow SQL queries, warnings in amber and errors in red. The statement of a slow SQL query is highlighted the same way as in the __TRILIUM_PH_0__SQL Console__TRILIUM_PH_1__, using the color scheme of code notes (see __TRILIUM_PH_2__Color schemes__TRILIUM_PH_3__ in __TRILIUM_PH_4__Code__TRILIUM_PH_5__).
units.context: Backend (server) logs > Accessing via the backend log

units.source: A search that the app runs in the background, for example to filter a collection, or that a script runs is followed by a __TRILIUM_PH_0__ line with its query and the number of notes it returned. The query is highlighted the same way as in a __TRILIUM_PH_1__Saved Search__TRILIUM_PH_2__. Quick search and saved searches don't add this line.
units.context: Backend (server) logs > Accessing via the backend log

units.source: Interaction since v0.104.0:
units.context: Backend (server) logs > Accessing via the backend log

units.source: The file can be downloaded as a text file using the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ button in the __TRILIUM_PH_1__Note menu__TRILIUM_PH_2__ area.
units.context: Backend (server) logs > Accessing via the backend log

units.source: The file can also be searched just like a normal __TRILIUM_PH_0__Code__TRILIUM_PH_1__ note.
units.context: Backend (server) logs > Accessing via the backend log

units.source: Location on the disk__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Backend (server) logs > Location on the disk

units.source: Backend logs are stored on the file system. To find them, open the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Data directory__TRILIUM_PH_1__, go to the __TRILIUM_PH_2__ subdirectory and find the latest log file, e.g. __TRILIUM_PH_3__.
units.context: Backend (server) logs > Location on the disk

units.source: In the terminal__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Backend (server) logs > In the terminal

units.source: The server also prints every log entry to its standard output, which is what __TRILIUM_PH_0__ or __TRILIUM_PH_1__ show. When that output is a terminal, each entry starts with its time and is colored like the backend log in the app: request status codes by class, slow SQL queries, warnings in yellow and errors in red. The statement of a slow SQL query and the query of a search are shown without syntax highlighting there. The startup banner with the Trilium logo and version information is colored too. Output to a file, a pipe or a container log stays plain text without the time, since those tools add their own.
units.context: Backend (server) logs > In the terminal

units.source: To turn the colors off in a terminal, set the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ environment variable; to force them on elsewhere, set __TRILIUM_PH_1__.
units.context: Backend (server) logs > In the terminal

units.source: Reporting backend bugs__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Backend (server) logs > Reporting backend bugs

units.source: You can attach the whole file to the bug report (preferable) or open it and copy-paste only the last lines / lines you believe are relevant.
units.context: Backend (server) logs > Reporting backend bugs

units.source: Customizing the retention of logs__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Backend (server) logs > Customizing the retention of logs

units.source: The backend logs are fully managed by the Trilium server. By default the last 90 days worth of logs are kept; the logs older than that are deleted in order to reduce the space consumption.
units.context: Backend (server) logs > Customizing the retention of logs

units.source: It's possible to change the retention period by modifying the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Configuration (config.ini or environment variables)__TRILIUM_PH_1__ via the __TRILIUM_PH_2__ file:
units.context: Backend (server) logs > Customizing the retention of logs

units.source: Or via the environment variable __TRILIUM_PH_0__.
units.context: Backend (server) logs > Customizing the retention of logs

units.source: Special cases:
units.context: Backend (server) logs > Customizing the retention of logs

units.source: Positive values indicate the number of days worth of logs to keep
units.context: Backend (server) logs > Customizing the retention of logs

units.source: A value of 0 results with the default value (90 days) to be used
units.context: Backend (server) logs > Customizing the retention of logs

units.source: Negative values (e.g. __TRILIUM_PH_0__) result with all logs to be kept, irrespective how ancient and numerous (and
units.context: Backend (server) logs > Customizing the retention of logs

units.source: If you set the retention days to a low number, you might notice that not all the log files are being deleted. This is because a minimum number of logs (7 at the time of writing) is maintained at all times.
units.context: Backend (server) logs > Customizing the retention of logs
